root_cause.text: The per-IO canceled flag (`UBLK_IO_FLAG_CANCELED`) was being reset only after all IOs in a queue were fetched, rather than immediately upon each individual IO fetch, causing fetched IOs to retain their canceled flag and preventing proper cancellation completion when the ublk server dies mid-recovery.
root_cause.evidence: The patch shows that `ublk_queue_reset_io_flags()` previously looped through all IOs in a queue to clear their canceled flags together, but this function is never called if the server dies before fetching all IOs. The fix introduces `ublk_reset_io_flags()` which clears the canceled flag for each individual IO immediately when it is fetched via `ublk_mark_io_ready()`, ensuring that even partially-fetched IOs can be properly canceled. The commit message explicitly states: "the per-IO canceled flags for all IOs in a queue are reset together only once all IOs for that queue have been fetched. So if a nonempty proper subset of the IOs for a queue are fetched when the ublk server dies, the IOs in that subset will never successfully be canceled, as their canceled flags remain set."

intent_record.intent_summary: Refactor IO flag reset logic by extracting per-IO flag clearing into a dedicated helper function and decoupling it from queue-level state reset.
intent_record.what: Extracted the per-IO flag reset logic into a new helper function `ublk_reset_io_flags()` that clears UBLK_IO_FLAG_CANCELED under spinlock protection. Modified `ublk_queue_reset_io_flags()` to remove the loop that iterates through all IOs and instead only reset queue-level state. Updated `ublk_mark_io_ready()` signature to accept an additional `struct ublk_io *io` parameter.
intent_record.how: This change separates concerns by moving individual IO flag clearing into a dedicated function that can be called per-IO with proper synchronization. The queue reset function now only manages queue-level state (canceling flag, fail_io flag) without touching individual IO flags. This enables per-IO flag reset to be called at different points in the code path, likely during IO completion or preparation, rather than bulk-resetting all IOs at once.

intent_record.intent_summary: Reset I/O flags when marking an I/O operation as ready to prevent stale flag state from affecting subsequent operations.
intent_record.what: Added a call to `ublk_reset_io_flags(ubq, io)` immediately after incrementing `ubq->nr_io_ready++` in the `ublk_mark_io_ready()` function.
intent_record.how: This change ensures that I/O flags are reset for each I/O operation when it is marked as ready. Previously, I/O flags were not being cleared at this point, which could leave stale flag state from previous operations, potentially causing incorrect behavior in subsequent I/O processing.

intent_record.intent_summary: Pass the I/O request context to ublk_mark_io_ready() to enable proper per-request handling and fix incomplete I/O state management.
intent_record.what: The function call to `ublk_mark_io_ready()` on line 3205 is modified to pass an additional third argument `io` to the function, changing from `ublk_mark_io_ready(ub, q_id)` to `ublk_mark_io_ready(ub, q_id, io)`.
intent_record.how: This change passes the `io` object (which represents the I/O request context) to the `ublk_mark_io_ready()` function. The function can now access and operate on the specific I/O request being processed, rather than only having access to the device and queue identifiers. This enables the function to perform I/O-specific operations or validations that were previously unavailable.

intent_record.intent_summary: Pass the I/O context to ublk_mark_io_ready() to ensure the function has access to the specific I/O request being marked as ready.
intent_record.what: Added a third argument `io` to the `ublk_mark_io_ready()` function call on line 3618, changing from two arguments to three arguments.
intent_record.how: The function now receives the `io` object as an additional parameter, allowing `ublk_mark_io_ready()` to access or operate on the specific I/O context that was just prepared in the batch preparation routine. This enables the function to perform operations that require knowledge of the individual I/O request being marked as ready.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly addresses the vulnerability root cause by refactoring the IO flag reset logic. The core issue is that the per-IO canceled flag (UBLK_IO_FLAG_CANCELED) was not being reset immediately upon each individual IO fetch. By extracting per-IO flag clearing into a dedicated helper function and decoupling it from queue-level state reset, this change enables the per-IO flag to be reset at the appropriate granularity (per-IO rather than per-queue), which is the exact fix needed to resolve the vulnerability.

The group directly addresses the core issue by resetting I/O flags when marking operations as ready, which aligns with the vulnerability's root cause of flags not being reset at the proper time (immediately upon IO fetch rather than after all IOs are fetched). This change ensures stale canceled flags don't persist on individual IOs.

The vulnerability stems from the canceled flag being reset at the queue level rather than per-IO. By passing individual I/O request context to ublk_mark_io_ready(), this change enables proper per-request handling and state management, allowing the canceled flag to be reset immediately upon each individual IO fetch rather than after all IOs are fetched. This is the structural change needed to fix the improper cancellation completion issue.

bic_trace_step.reason: This commit moves ublk_mark_io_ready() out of __ublk_fetch() and into the callers (ublk_fetch and ublk_batch_prep_io) after spinlocks are released. The diff shows: (1) removal of ublk_mark_io_ready() call from __ublk_fetch() at line 3067, (2) addition of ublk_mark_io_ready() in ublk_fetch() after ublk_config_io_buf() completes and mutex is still held but before mutex_unlock(), and (3) addition of ublk_mark_io_ready() in ublk_batch_prep_io() after ublk_io_unlock(io) releases the spinlock. The vulnerable construct (calling ublk_mark_io_ready() while holding a spinlock that prevents proper mutex acquisition) is being fixed by moving the call outside the critical sections. This is a fix commit, not a bug-introducing commit.
